To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) regulated secretory proteins are not sorted into secretory granule vesicles in the TGN; (2) the regulated secretory proteins aggregate in the TGN to form a ‘sorting platform’; (3) aggregation of the regulated secretory protein is required to initiate sorting of secretory granular proteins; and (4) the sorting platform is a dynamic structure which is assembled and disassembled in response to changes in the secretory pathway.

(1) sorting of proteins into secretory granule occurs in the trans-Goli network; (2) sorting is a multistep process which includes aggregation, binding to the secretory granules and exclusion of non- secretory granule proteins.
the sorting of proteins into nascent regulated secretory granules occurs by a mechanism which involves aggregation of the secretory proteins and the formation of a protein complex in the TGN.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sorting events in secretory protein transport from the TGN are not yet understood, and that much work is needed to elucidate the mechanisms which govern the formation of secretory granular compartments.
sorting of secretory granulate components occurs at multiple sites in the secretory pathway, and that the precise sequence of events is not yet clear.
the sorting events in secretory-granule biogenesis in the TGN remain a mystery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the TGN is the site of the initial sorting of proteins destined for secretory granules and that the sorting is mediated by the interaction of the cytosolic domains of the secretory proteins with cytosolic proteins.
the TGN is a sorting station for the formation of secretory granular proteins.
the TGN is a dynamic compartment where secretory granule assembly occurs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

secretory granule biogenesis is not only a complex process involving multiple steps and multiple players, but also a dynamic process which is constantly changing in response to physiological stimuli and to the needs of the cell.

the sorting of proteins into secretory granule occurs at the level of TGN and that this sorting is not a random process, but is mediated by specific signals in the secreted proteins and by specific receptors.
the trans-Golgic network is the site of secretory granulation and that this site is dynamic and highly regulated.
